newsitem.title: USA: TWA sees worse Q2 financial performance.
newsitem.headline: TWA sees worse Q2 financial performance.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc, the nation's seventh-largest air carrier, said Monday it expects its second quarter financial performance will be worse than its results during the same period last year.

"The company's unit revenues, yields and cash position continue to be adversely affected by the negative impact on consumer demand created by the previous deterioration in operating performance," it said in a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. It said the Flight 800 crash last year "distracted management's attention from core operating issues and led to lost bookings and revenues."

In late 1996, St. Louis'based TWA said its management began to implement a series of actions to boost the airline's performance, including ending a maintenance contract with the government, restructuring New York services and continuing its replacement of 747 and L-1011 fleets by the end of 1997.

"The company believes that operating and financial results at (New York airport) JFK will be improved by the company's recently announced plancs to accelerate retirement of its remaining 747 and L-1011 fleets to year-end 1997," the company said, adding that they will be replaced by smaller, more efficient new or later-model used 757s, 767s and MD80s.
Even so, TWA said its second quarter results will be worse than the year-earlier period and follow first quarter results that "compare unfavorably" with the first quarter of 1996.

TWA's operating revenue of $762.3 million during the first quarter of 1997 represented a $20.1 million decrease from the first quarter of 1996, when the company's operating revenue totaled $782.4 million.

The company said reduced revenue during the first quarter reflected a planned reduction in passenger capacity because larger aircraft were replaced with smaller planes. In addition, fuel costs during the first quarter increased by 11.2 percent.

As a result, the company said it experienced an operating loss of $99.5 million and a net loss of $71.6 million during the first quarter, which compares with an operating loss of $54.2 million and a net loss of $37.1 million during the first quarter of 1996.
